arxiv-2101-06890.title: Cooperative and Competitive Biases for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Conference: Proc. of the 20th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2021); May 3–7, 2021; Online 94
arxiv-2101-06890.creator: Heechang Ryu, Hayong Shin, Jinkyoo Park ∗ \ast
arxiv-2101-06890.description: Abstract . Training a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm is more challenging than training a single-agent reinforcement learning algorithm, because the result of a multi-agent task strongly depends on the complex interactions among agents and their interactions with a stochastic and dynamic environment.

arxiv-2106-06923.title: How fast do microdroplets generated during liquid-liquid phase separation move in a confined 2D space?
arxiv-2106-06923.creator: Gilmar F. Arends, John M. Shaw, Xuehua Zhang
arxiv-2106-06923.description: Abstract How liquid transport occurs in confined spaces is relevant to many industrial and lab-scale processes, ranging from enhanced oil recovery to drug delivery systems. In this work, we investigate propelling microdroplets that form from liquid-liquid phase separation in a quasi-2D chamber, focusing on the direction and speed of microdroplets in response to local composition gradients.

arxiv-2311-00369.title: Direct System Identification of Dynamical Networks with Partial Measurements: a Maximum Likelihood Approach
arxiv-2311-00369.creator: João Victor Galvão da Mata, Anders Hansson, Martin S. Andersen
arxiv-2311-00369.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel direct approach to system identification of dynamic networks with missing data based on maximum likelihood estimation. Dynamic networks generally present a singular probability density function, which poses a challenge in the estimation of their parameters.

arxiv-2401-17453.title: Flat, Uniformly Expanding Space in five Exercises
arxiv-2401-17453.creator: Bernd A. Berg
arxiv-2401-17453.description: Abstract Abstract Exercises with solutions are presented which should allow advanced undergraduate students to understand properties of a flat, uniformly expanding space. No knowledge of general or special relativity is needed besides that the speed of light c is a constant.

arxiv-2405-05120.title: GRB afterglows with energy injections in AGN accretion disks
arxiv-2405-05120.creator: Bao-Quan Huang, Tong Liu, Xiao-Yan Li, Yun-Feng Wei
arxiv-2405-05120.description: Abstract Active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks are widely considered potential hosts for various high-energy transients, including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). The reactivation of GRB central engines can provide additional energy to shocks formed during the interaction of the initially ejected GRB jets with the circumburst material, commonly referred to as energy injections.

arxiv-2409-11792.title: A no-go theorem for sequential and retro-causal hidden-variable theories based on computational complexity.
arxiv-2409-11792.creator: Doriano Brogioli
arxiv-2409-11792.description: Abstract The celebrated Bell’s no-go theorem rules out the hidden-variable theories falling in the hypothesis of locality and causality, by requiring the theory to model the quantum correlation-at-a-distance phenomena. Here I develop an independent no-go theorem, by inspecting the ability of a theory to model quantum circuits .

arxiv-2506-08518.title: FEDTAIL: Federated Long-Tailed Domain Generalization with Sharpness-Guided Gradient Matching
arxiv-2506-08518.creator: Sunny Gupta, Nikita Jangid, Shounak Das, Amit Sethi
arxiv-2506-08518.description: Abstract Domain Generalization (DG) seeks to train models that perform reliably on unseen target domains without access to target data during training. While recent progress in smoothing the loss landscape has improved generalization, existing methods often falter under long-tailed class distributions and conflicting optimization objectives.

arxiv-2508-00387.title: STF: Shallow-Level Temporal Feedback to Enhance Spiking Transformers
arxiv-2508-00387.creator: Zeqi Zheng, Zizheng Zhu, Yingchao Yu, Yanchen Huang, Changze Lv, Junfeng Tang, Zhaofei Yu, Yaochu Jin
arxiv-2508-00387.description: Abstract Transformer-based Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) suffer from a great performance gap compared to floating-point Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) due to the binary nature of spike trains. Recent efforts have introduced deep-level feedback loops to transmit high-level semantic information to narrow this gap.

pmc-10666498.creator: Rashmi Dhital, Ashbina Pokharel, Ioannis Karageorgiou, Dilli R Poudel, Monica Guma, Kenneth Kalunian
pmc-10666498.description: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients are prone to frequent emergency department (ED) visits. pmc-11345194.title: Case report: A novel mutation of the CAPN3 gene in a Chinese family with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2A
pmc-11345194.creator: Wanjun Feng, Yanyan Cao, Ruolin Ren, Xiaohui Yang, Chunyan Cao, Hongwei Jiang, Ganqin Du
pmc-11345194.description: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2A (LGMD R1 Calpain 3-Related, LGMD2A/R1), an autosomal recessive disorder, is characterized by progressive muscle weakness with a prominent presentation in the proximal limb girdle muscles. LGMD2A/R1, which is caused by variants in calcium-activated neutral proteinase 3 (CAPN3), is the most common.

pmc-11548766.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Iris Segmentation on Benchmarking Datasets
pmc-11548766.creator: Mst Rumana Sumi, Priyanka Das, Afzal Hossain, Soumyabrata Dey, Stephanie Schuckers, Euntai Kim, Sangyoun Lee, Kang Ryoung Park, Eui Chul Lee
pmc-11548766.description: Iris is one of the most widely used biometric modalities because of its uniqueness, high matching performance, and inherently secure nature. Iris segmentation is an essential preliminary step for iris-based biometric authentication. The authentication accuracy is directly connected with the iris segmentation accuracy.

pmc-11569378.title: MicroRNA-mediated autophagy and drug resistance in cancer: mechanisms and therapeutic strategies
pmc-11569378.creator: Jinxing Wei, Xianghui Wang, Duo Yu, Yanyang Tu, Yaoyu Yu
pmc-11569378.description: This paper provides an exhaustive overview of the intricate interplay between microRNAs (miRNAs) and autophagy in the context of human cancers, underscoring the pivotal role these non-coding RNAs play in modulating autophagic pathways and their implications for cancer development, progression, and resistance to therapy.

pmc-11681481.title: Neutrophil Activation and Adhesiveness in Coronary Artery Disease: Results From the COLCHICINE‐PCI Biomarker Substudy

pmc-13084961.title: Assessing patient perspectives on enrollment in lymphoma clinical trials
pmc-13084961.creator: Neha Akkad, Minxing Chen, Sophia Nguyen, Alexis Romero, Lynne Nguyen, Lorna H. McNeill, Loretta J. Nastoupil, Jason Westin, Paolo Strati, Sairah Ahmed, Liliana Vallejo, Rebeca Yzquierdo, Amy Ayers, Christopher R. Flowers, Chijioke Nze
pmc-13084961.description: BackgroundClinical trials drive advances in lymphoma care, yet certain patient groups including socioeconomically disadvantaged, racial/ethnic groups, and women remain underrepresented. Given limited/inconsistent data regarding solutions to improve clinical trial enrollment of these groups, the authors performed a study to assess patient perspectives on barriers to enrollment and define priorities for future interventions.

pmc-13123705.title: Two new factors modulating Bacillus subtilis spore resistance and germination
pmc-13123705.creator: William J. Bannon, Dejalee Padilla, Dhruv Suryadevara, Faith Ye, George Korza, James Wicander, Peter Setlow
pmc-13123705.description: New effectors of spore properties have been identified in two Bacillus subtilis strains—bacillithiol, the major low-molecular-weight thiol in B. subtilis, and sporulene, a multi-ring compound synthesized from curcumene in spores’ outer layers. The absence of either bacillithiol or sporulene caused faster germination of spores of one wild-type B.

pmc-13391324.title: Social capital and educational justice as predictors of civic engagement in higher education: the mediating roles of institutional trust and student empowerment
pmc-13391324.creator: Marian Mae S. Sapanta, Romel C. Mutya
pmc-13391324.description: Aligning with the Philippine Commission on Higher Education’s mission to produce socially responsible and civically active graduates, this study examined college students’ academic experiences in relation to social capital, educational justice, student empowerment, institutional trust, and civic engagement. A survey was conducted among 1,026 college students from selected state universities in Northern Cebu, Philippines.

pmc-13408451.title: CMFGP-Net: RGBT salient object detection based on cross-modal feature global perception and multi-scale deformable convolution fusion
pmc-13408451.creator: Lijuan Shi, Haitang Li, Qiuju Liu
pmc-13408451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aiming at the challenges of insufficient multi-modal feature interaction, spatial-spectral misalignment, and poor robustness to target deformation and occlusion in RGB-T salient object detection, this paper proposes a detection framework (CMFGP-Net) based on cross-modal global perception and multi-scale cross-fusion. The framework adopts Swin Transformer with a hierarchical window attention mechanism as the backbone network, which significantly enhances the global context modeling capability.

pmc-13595560.title: A tumor microenvironment acid-responsive therapy combining fenton chemistry and chemotherapy via TNF pathway for synergistic and safe lung cancer treatment
pmc-13595560.creator: Cai Zhang, Long Zhang, Jing Tian, Jie Shi, Xiao Li, Tong Jiao, Xin Zhao, Bo Yuan, Lizhong Zeng, Yuanyuan Cheng, Umid Sunnatovich Mamedov, Laziz Nurkhonovich Niyazov, Shuanying Yang
pmc-13595560.description: Lung cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors, but traditional treatments, particularly chemotherapy, often face significant challenges, including drug resistance and high systemic toxicity. In this study, we developed a novel acid responsive nanoparticle, La₂O₃@PDA/PTX, by combining lanthanum oxide (La₂O₃), polydopamine (PDA), and paclitaxel (PTX). This nanoparticle demonstrated excellent aqueous stability, high biocompatibility, and low toxicity.

pmc-13625650.title: Children’s independent mobility in Japan: travelling to, returning from, and playing within local parks
pmc-13625650.creator: Tomoko Doi Hata, Tomoya Ohyama, Jenny Veitch, Daisuke Takagi
pmc-13625650.description: Children's independent mobility (CIM), a parental permission for children to travel and play at a destination without adult supervision, is considered essential for supporting both the physical and psychological well-being of children. Of the various places CIM can be granted, the present study focused on local parks as a destination.
